name: Expanding Horizons
summary: Thundris Windweaver sends word from Auberdine across the Great Sea to Stormwind. The letter asks City Architect Baros Alexston to recognize Auberdine's work and its home.

sections.title: Bridging Two Hemispheres
sections.body: Auberdine now links Darkshore to Stormwind by sea. Night elves once kept to Kalimdor's forests, apart from the Eastern Kingdoms, but after the Third War they joined the Grand Alliance. The new passage gives the northern port a direct tie to the human kingdom. Local leaders want the shipping route secured and Auberdine connected to the wider Alliance. Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, ruined cities nearby, have long drawn more notice than the living coastal settlement.

sections.title: A Missive to the City Architect
sections.body: The letter crossing the Great Sea is addressed to Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect. He oversees construction and infrastructure in the human capital, including public works and logistics. Thundris Windweaver wants Auberdine's work recognized and its home made known.

faq.q: Who sends you on this quest?
faq.answer: Thundris Windweaver, an influential night elf in Auberdine, asks you to carry the letter. He feels the settlement is overlooked by Darnassus and by allies across the ocean, and seeks a formal link with the human kingdom.

Baros Alexston is Stormwind's City Architect. He is a respected civic planner who knew Edwin VanCleef when they were younger, and oversees construction and structural administration throughout the capital.

faq.q: Why is Auberdine reaching out to Stormwind?
faq.answer: Auberdine wants its harbor recognized as a gateway for supplies, commerce, and Alliance travel. Local leaders hope the new sea routes between Darkshore and the Eastern Kingdoms will strengthen economic and logistical ties with the human kingdom.

faq.q: How does travel work between Auberdine and Stormwind?
aliases: how to get to stormwind from auberdine
faq.answer: A vessel now sails from Auberdine across the Great Sea to Stormwind Harbor, bringing supplies and life to Auberdine's shores.

Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran were prosperous highborne cities in ancient Darkshore. The Great Sundering shattered the continent ten thousand years ago, and the cities now lie in haunted ruins, more prominent in kaldorei history than living villages like Auberdine.

faq.q: Why deliver this to an architect instead of King Anduin or Bolvar?
faq.answer: Thundris Windweaver gives no reason for his choice. He asks you to take the letter to Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect, so Auberdine's work can be recognized.

angles.text: For the kaldorei, opening sea routes to the Eastern Kingdoms breaks with ten thousand years of seclusion and binds your people to human civilization.
As a human, you see the reach of the rebuilt kingdom grow when you return to Stormwind carrying a kaldorei settlement's seal.
As an Alliance member, you see the work needed to unite peoples across two continents into one faction.
